newsitem.title: BELGIUM: SOCCER-LEEKENS TAKES CHARGE AS BELGIUM SACK VAN MOER.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-LEEKENS TAKES CHARGE AS BELGIUM SACK VAN MOER.

text.p: Belgium soccer coach Wilfried Van Moer has been sacked after just nine months in charge and replaced by Georges Leekens who leaves surprise first division leaders Mouscron, a soccer union spokesman said on Tuesday.

Spokesman Guido Dewindt said Van Moer was sacked principally because of Belgium's humiliating 3-0 home defeat by the Netherlands in a World Cup qualifier last month and also because of communication problems with players and the media.
"It's Belgium-Netherlands," Dewindt told Reuters. "(The union) has thought it over, what had happened, whether tactical mistakes had been made.

"A coach depends on results and losing at home against the Netherlands, a key match, endangered our World Cup participation. Now we have to win the next two away games to stay in the running for second place in the group."
Belgium, bidding to qualify for their fifth consecutive World Cup finals, are third in European qualifying group seven, behind the Netherlands and Wales.
They won their first two matches, against Turkey and San Marino, before losing to the Dutch.
They visit Wales in March and Turkey in April.

Dewindt said former Belgium defender Leekens will become full-time coach with immediate effect and quit first division fledglings Mouscron, who have a four-point first division lead over title holders Club Brugge.

"This is perhaps the most difficult challenge I ever accepted," Leekens told BRTN radio. "It will be tough but I'm full of confidence. I hope that we will get that national, patriotic feeling back again."
His first mission will be to groom Belgium for a friendly against Northern Ireland in Belfast on February 11.
Leekens's contract runs at least until after the European championship finals in 2000, which are organised jointly by Belgium and the Netherlands.
Van Moer was assistant coach to Paul Van Himst until April last year when Van Himst was sacked after a run of poor results and friction with players.
Van Moer was initially praised for his no-nonsense approach but was later criticised for his surly attitude towards players and reporters.
He was also slammed for dropping key players including Philippe Albert and Marc Degryse in his first matches.
"One thing leads to another. If you win and you have communication problems you can accept it. But if you lose you look at other aspects too," Dewindt said.
Leekens has coached a string of Belgian first division teams including Club Brugge and Anderlecht. He also managed Trabzonspor of Turkey.
